title: Been there, done that!
goals: Talk about life experiences with the present perfect and irregular past participles.
Say how many times with ever, never, always, once, twice and many times.
Tell when to use the present perfect and when to use the simple past.
Tell been and gone apart when you talk about trips.
Keep the conversation going with echo questions (Do you? Have you? Did you?).
Show your attitude with fortunately, unfortunately and amazingly when writing a travel blog.

learn.title: Present perfect: form and past participles
learn.html:
The present perfect talks about experiences or actions at an unspecified time in the past: it doesn't matter when it happened, what matters is that it already happened. Form: have / has + past participle.

AffirmativeNegativeQuestion
I've traveled in Asia.I haven't been to Paris.Have you seen that movie?
He's surfed in Hawaii.She hasn't tried surfing.Has she gone sailing?

With he / she / it, use has ('s) and hasn't.

Regular participles = same as the past form, with -ed: travel → traveled, try → tried. Irregular (you have to memorize them):

BasePastPast participle
bewas / werebeen
dodiddone
gowentgone
havehadhad
seesawseen
taketooktaken
forgetforgotforgotten
breakbrokebroken
winwonwon
loselostlost

been vs. gone: I've been to Paris = I went there and came back. She's gone to Paris = she left and is still there.

watch.why: After have comes the past participle (gone), not the past form (went).
The past participle of break is broken.

learn.title: Ever, never, always, once, twice, many times
learn.html:
These expressions go with the present perfect to say how many times something has happened, or whether it has ever happened.

ExpressionExample
ever (in questions: at any time)Have you ever gone white-water rafting?
never … (before) (not at any time)I've never gone rafting. She's never tried it before.
always (all the time, and still true)I've always wanted to study acting.
once / twice / three times / many times / a few times / a couple of timesWe've gone sailing twice. He's seen it many times.

Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. (with he/she: Yes, she has. / No, she hasn't.) Never is already negative: don't use not with never.

watch.wrong: Have you ever go to Spain?
watch.right: Have you ever been to Spain?
watch.why: After have comes the past participle.

watch.wrong: She has seen that movie two times ago.
watch.right: She has seen that movie twice.
watch.why: Ago goes with the simple past; with the present perfect, use twice / two times.

learn.title: Present perfect vs. simple past
learn.html:
Present perfect: experiences, without saying when (Have you ever gone rafting? Yes, I have.).

Simple past: when you give a date, a specific time or details of the event (I went rafting last May. Did you have a good time?).

General questionAnswer with details
Have you ever won a prize?Yes, I have. I won a contest last year.
Has she ever lost her phone?Yes, she has. She lost it on a bus last week.

With words for a finished time (yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago, when) you always use the simple past.

watch.wrong: Did you ever try rock climbing?
watch.right: Have you ever tried rock climbing?

watch.wrong: When have you gone to Oaxaca?
watch.right: When did you go to Oaxaca?
watch.why: When asks about a moment: simple past.

learn.title: Attitude adverbs: fortunately, unfortunately, amazingly
learn.html:
They show how you feel about what you are saying. They usually go at the start of the sentence, followed by a comma, or at the end.

AdverbUse it when…Example
Fortunatelyyou are happy about what happenedFortunately, there were some great guides.
Unfortunatelyyou regret what happened or didn't happenI didn't see a quetzal bird, unfortunately.
Amazinglyyou are happy and surprisedAmazingly, it wasn't really scary.

watch.why: It's an adverb: it ends in -ly.
Losing your passports is bad: unfortunately.

learn.title: Strategy: echo questions (Do you? / Have you?)
learn.html:
To show interest and keep the conversation going, reply with a short question in the same tense the other person used, and then ask a question.

Says AReplies B
I like hip-hop. (simple present)Do you? What kind?
I've seen that movie twice. (present perfect)Have you? Did you like it?
We went to a new club. (simple past)Did you? How was it?
She can swim well. (can)Can she?

More informal and with surprise: You do? You have? You did? (the voice goes up). Other reactions: Wow. I'm impressed! I've heard good things about it.

learn.title: Useful expressions for talking about experiences
learn.html:
• Have you ever …? — asking about experiences.
  • Yes, I have. I … last year. — answering and giving details in the past.
  • No, never. / No, I haven't. Not yet. — negative answer.
  • I've always wanted to … — talking about a dream.
  • Do you? / Have you? / Did you? — showing interest.
  • I'm impressed! / Wow, that sounds amazing. — reacting.
  • I've heard good things about it. How was it? — keeping the conversation going.
  • Fortunately, … / Unfortunately, … — giving your attitude.

write.prompt: Write a text of 120 to 180 words about your adventure or travel experiences. Say three things you have done (with frequency words such as once, twice or never before), one thing you have never done and have always wanted to do, and use the simple past to give details about one of them (when and how it happened). Include an attitude adverb. Opening example: I've traveled a lot in Mexico, but I've never been to…
checklist: At least 4 sentences in the present perfect with the correct have / has
Correctly formed past participles (been, gone, seen…)
One frequency expression (once, twice, many times) and one never
Details of an experience in the simple past, with a date (last May…)
Fortunately / Unfortunately / Amazingly, followed by a comma
write.model:
I've traveled a lot in Mexico, but I've never been to the Copper Canyon, and I've always wanted to go there. I've visited Oaxaca twice, and I've been to Mexico City many times because my cousins live there. I've seen the ocean in Cancun once, and I've also gone camping in the mountains near Puebla. I've never traveled by plane outside the country, but I hope to do it soon.

My best experience was my first trip to Oaxaca. I went there last May with two friends. We took an overnight bus, and we arrived very early in the morning. Amazingly, we found a small hotel for only 300 pesos a night. On the second day, we visited the ruins of Monte Alban, and I took more than a hundred photos. Unfortunately, it rained in the afternoon, so we went back to the hotel and played cards.

I have never eaten so much delicious food in one weekend! Fortunately, my friends love traveling as much as I do, so we are planning another trip for next year.

write.prompt: Write an 8-line dialogue between two friends talking about experiences. Use Have you ever…? questions, at least three echo questions (Do you? Have you? Did you?), and one follow-up question in the simple past. Opening example: A: I've been to Oaxaca three times. B: Have you? …
checklist: Two Have you ever + past participle questions
Three echo questions in the correct tense
One answer with details in the simple past
write.model:
A: I've been to Oaxaca three times.
B: Have you? Wow, I'm impressed! When did you go for the first time?
A: I went in 2019 with my sister. We visited Monte Alban and ate a lot of mole.
B: Did you? I've never tried real mole. Have you ever cooked it at home?
A: Yes, I have, but it was a disaster! I burned the sauce last Christmas.
B: Did you? That's funny! I burned rice once. Have you ever taken a cooking class?
A: No, I haven't. I've always wanted to, though.
B: Really? Well, I've never taken one either. Let's sign up together!

reading.title: Three days in Chiapas
reading.intro: Read this travel blog and answer the questions.
paragraphs: Hi, everyone! I'm back from my first big adventure trip, and I want to tell you all about it. I've always wanted to visit Chiapas, and last month I finally went with my cousin Elena. We stayed for three days, and we did more than I ever imagined.

On the first day we visited the waterfalls of Agua Azul. Amazingly, the water really is blue! Elena has been there twice, but for me it was the first time. We took a lot of photos, and I swam for an hour. Unfortunately, I forgot my sunglasses, and the sun was very strong.

On the second day we went white-water rafting. I've never been a brave person, and I was scared at first. A guide gave us a helmet and explained everything slowly. Fortunately, our guide was very patient, and in the end it wasn't scary at all. I fell off the raft once, but I laughed about it later. Have you ever gone rafting? If you haven't, you should try it.

On the last day we visited the ruins of Palenque. We had a beautiful view of the jungle from the top of the temple. I've seen many pyramids in books, but I've never seen anything like that in person. We also rode a zip line over the trees. Elena had done it before, but I hadn't, and I screamed the whole time.

Of course, the trip wasn't perfect. We got a flat tire on the way back, and we waited almost two hours for help. Still, it was a great trip, and I've already started planning the next one. I've heard good things about Oaxaca and the Yucatán, so maybe I'll go there next year. Where have you been this year? Write to me in the comments, and tell me your favorite place!

listening.title: Have you ever…?
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between two friends. You can replay it.

lines.text: Hey, Pablo! Did you have a good vacation?
It was amazing! I went to Baja California and I went kayaking for the first time.
Did you? I've never been kayaking. Was it difficult?
A little. I fell into the water twice, but fortunately the water was warm.
Wow. Have you ever gone surfing too?
Yes, I have. I've gone surfing a few times in Oaxaca.
Have you? I've always wanted to try it. Is it scary?
Not really. Unfortunately, I'm not very good at it. And you? Have you done anything exciting this year?
Well, I went hot air ballooning in Teotihuacán last March.
You did? That's incredible! How was it?
Beautiful. I've been afraid of heights all my life, but amazingly, I loved it.
I'm impressed! Let's go on a trip together next summer.
